items.name: Vata Soft Rice Root Mung Bowl

ingredients.name: Carrots, peeled and cut into small cubes
Sweet potato, peeled and cut into small cubes

steps: Prepare 1250 ml (about 5 1/4 cups) hot water before starting Vata Soft Rice Root Mung Bowl; keep one small ladle in reserve in case the base tightens early.

Warm cumin in ghee and coat the rinsed rice and split mung in the fragrant fat. Give the spices about 30 seconds before adding the larger pieces, then continue over medium-low heat for 3–4 minutes, moving the pan often, until the raw aroma is gone.

Add both kinds of root cubes and hot water, then cook under a lid until the grains and vegetables are very soft. Maintain gentle medium heat for 20–22 minutes, stirring every 5 minutes, until a grain pressed between two fingers has no chalky center.
Inspect the main component at minute 17; rotate the pot and add 30–60 ml hot water only if the base is tightening before it is tender.

Stir the bowl to a cohesive, moist texture, season it, and rest it covered before serving. Leave the pan off the flame for 6 minutes, then taste and correct the final balance before serving at the stated temperature.
Fluff or stir Vata Soft Rice Root Mung Bowl once after its off-heat rest, check the final consistency, and serve it warm without prolonged holding.

steps: Heat 1300 ml (about 5 1/2 cups) water until vigorously boiling, then lower it to a bare simmer beside the main pot for measured additions.

For Pitta Artichoke Chickpea Barley, cover the pearled barley and chickpeas with at least three times its volume of cool water and soak for 8–12 hours; drain for 2 minutes before the first heated step.

Cook the soaked chickpeas until almost tender, then add the barley and diced fennel bulb. Use a pressure cooker at steady pressure for 25–30 minutes, or keep a covered pot at a gentle simmer for 60–75 minutes, until one bean mashes completely between two fingers.

Lower in the artichoke quarters once the grains begin to soften, and simmer until every component is tender. Maintain moderate heat for 12–14 minutes, stirring every 4 minutes, until a grain pressed between two fingers has no chalky center.
